section.sectionSummaryBrief: Daas brings resolution to choose good, transcending the indecision of intellect alone, as it draws from Kesser.
section.t: And the main aspect of daas is that through it, a decision about a matter is reached.
That is,
the discernment between good and evil,
“the wise discern between good and bad,”
can also be from the side of Chochmah and Binah,
but nevertheless,
he will not have a decision about what to do,
for from the side of intellect there can be rationales for this and for that.
And as is known,
the proof from the generation of the Flood,
that from that same rationale that necessitated there be a flood,
“for the inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth,”
afterward the conclusion was “I will not again continue to smite,” etc.,
“and there will no longer be a flood to destroy the earth.”
That is,
that from intellect itself one cannot come to a decision,
and only through daas, which enters into the depth of the matter,
can one then come to a decision about how to act.
And this is what is written,
“and you shall choose life,”
that is,
that even though it is already stated,
“See, I have placed before you… life and good and the opposite,”
nevertheless,
it is not satisfied with this,
and it says “and you shall choose life,”
and particularly according to what the Alter Rebbe said,
that the letters of “and you shall choose life” are a granting of power that the choice for life can be made,
from which it is understood that it is not sufficient that one knows that there is life and its opposite,
because from this very fact it could be that he will choose the opposite, G-d forbid,
therefore the command “and you shall choose life” is necessary,
and this is through the aspect of daas, as above.
But still, it needs to be understood,
how is it that through daas one can choose the good,
for since from the side of intellect,
even though “the wise discern between good and bad,”
nevertheless it could be that despite this he will choose the opposite,
and as it is written,
“they are wise to do evil,”
if so,
how will “and you shall choose life” come about through daas?
And the explanation of this is,
that daas connects Chochmah and Binah,
and thus daas itself is above Chochmah and Binah,
that is,
that daas receives from the aspect of Kesser,
as is known that in a place where daas is counted, Kesser is not counted,
that is,
that daas is in the place of Kesser,
and therefore from this aspect it is possible to have “and you shall choose life.”

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The ultimate knowledge of not knowing is a self-recognition of the soul in Atzmus Ein Sof, enabling the choice of good even for simple Jews.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter is,
that it is known that “the ultimate knowledge is that we do not know,”
and the simple explanation of this is,
that first one must understand all that is possible, and afterward one comes to the ultimate knowledge,
that one understands that in truth one does not know, etc.
But the inner explanation of this is,
that the ultimate knowledge is that the knowledge should be in that which we do not know,
that is,
that even the aspect of “we do not know” should be in the category of knowledge.
And the explanation of this is,
that,
there is knowledge of affirmation and knowledge of negation.
Knowledge of affirmation is in Binah,
which comes in a manner of comprehension,
that one grasps the intellect through perception and enclothing in seven aspects, etc.
And knowledge of negation is in Chochmah,
that is, one understands the intellect by negating from it the matters that oppose and contradict it.
Nevertheless, it is understood,
that even the thing grasped through knowledge of negation has a connection to the matters from which it is negated,
for they are at least within its category,
and therefore it is possible to negate it from them.
But there is another aspect of knowledge that does not come even through negation,
because the matter is not within the category of knowledge at all, such that we could grasp it through negation,
and this is the aspect of “we do not know.”
And the explanation of this in the comprehension of G-dliness is,
that,
there is the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin and the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin,
the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin is subject to knowledge of affirmation,
but regarding the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin, only knowledge of negation applies,
but nevertheless, this is within the category of worlds,
for it is called Sovev Kol Almin.
But there is an aspect that is above Sovev Kol Almin,
even above the general Sovev,
and even above the true essence of the aspect of Sovev,
where even knowledge of negation does not apply.
And it is like what is written in Shaar HaYichud VeHaEmunah,
that this is like one who says about some lofty and deep wisdom that it is impossible to touch it with hands because of the depth of the concept,
anyone who hears would laugh at him,
because the matter of wisdom is not within the category of touch at all,
even not in a way of negation.
And about this it is said, “the ultimate knowledge is that we do not know,”
that even in the aspect of “we do not know” there must be the matter of knowledge,
and it is that the essence of the soul recognizes the essence of Ein Sof
(essence grasps essence).
And like the analogy,
a small infant who still has smallness of daas or has no daas at all,
and nevertheless is drawn to his father,
this is not because of some rationale that he understands how he is his father, etc.,
but it is only an innate recognition, because he was born from him.
And this matter is drawn down also into the revealed faculties,
and it is the aspect of Daas Eloki, which is above Chochmah and Binah,
and from the side of Daas Eloki there can be the decision to choose good,
even though from the side of intellect it can be in a manner of “they are wise to do evil.”
And since the command “and you shall choose life” is for every single Jew,
it is understood that the power for this is given to every single Jew,
even to simple people who have no understanding or comprehension,
that is,
that the Daas Eloki from the side of the essence is drawn down to the lowest levels to every single Jew,
even to simple people,
that they too have the granting of power that there should be “and you shall choose life.”

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The inner aspect of daas enables separation of good and evil through self-recognition of Atzmus, while the eighth king Hadar, the foundation, is the source of rectification through avodah from below to above.
section.t: And all this is from the side of the inwardness of daas,
but from the side of the externality of daas there can be a mixture of good and evil,
and this is that the beginning of the shattering was in the aspect of daas,
for all the cause of the intermingling of good and evil is from the side of daas,
as above.
However,
also the matter of separation between good and evil and the refinement, where one chooses the good and separates the evil, is through daas,
except that this is from the supernal aspect of daas,
which is the matter of the innate recognition in the Essence of the Ein Sof light,
and this aspect and level is only in holiness.
And this is the matter of the eighth king,
Hadar,
about whom it is not said “and he died,”
because there was no aspect of shattering in him,
and he is the root and source of rectification.
And the explanation is,
that the eighth king is Yesod,
and Yesod is the middle line that is drawn from daas,
and as the saying, “there is no hardness except from daas,”
and on a higher level,
it draws from the aspect of Kesser,
for Kesser is drawn down to the end of the line,
and therefore we see that in the influence of the drop, the essence is drawn more than in the influence of daas and intellect,
and as explained from the proof that a blind person gives birth to a complete child, etc.
And because of this, “and he died” is not said about Hadar,
because in Yesod there was no aspect of shattering,
and on the contrary, it is the root and source of rectification,
which is the matter of refinement.
And in more detail,
in the matter of refinement itself there are two modes,
refinement from above to below,
and refinement from below to above.
And,
when the refinement is in a way of revelation of light from above,
it can be that sparks of holiness that were extinguished will be pushed away and not be refined,
and furthermore,
since the refinement is not from the power of the lower one,
it can be that after the light departs, the lower one will remain in his level and not be refined.
Therefore, the refinement must be in a way of avodah from below to above.
And this is that Yitzchak wanted to bless Esav,
that is, he wanted to draw upon him a supernal light, through which he would be refined in a passive manner,
and he erred in this,
for he would have been completely nullified,
and his rectification needed to be through Yaakov,
for then it is in a way of refinement.
And even though regarding Yaakov it is written “and he gave,” etc.,
“he gave and again gave,”
the intention is not that the refinement is through a revelation of light from above,
but rather this was only in a way of granting power,
and afterward the refinement must be in a way of avodah from below to above.
And this matter is accomplished specifically through daas.
